pages.title: Marking
pages.text: Switch the pointer to $(l)Mark$() mode (Ctrl + scroll), then sneak + right-click to mark in order:$(br)$(li)Work block: depot / basin / belt$(li)Input: a container$(li)Output: a container$(br)$(br)$(italic)Only blocks with an item handler count as containers. $()

pages.title: Applying to a maid
pages.text: When you're done, $(l)sneak + right-click the maid$(). The chat bar tells you which mode you got:$(br)$(li)$(l)Full logistics$(): work block + input + output$(li)$(l)Process-only$(): only the work block$(br)$(br)$(c)Only the work block is mandatory$().

pages.title: Process-only mode
pages.text: If you only mark a work block, she processes whatever $(l)you$() put on it — no fetching, no output transfer.$(br2)Handy when robots or belts handle the logistics and you just want her to do the hammering.$(br2)$(italic)Note: if the output can be processed again by the same tool (log → stripped → planks), she'll keep going and spend durability each step. $()

pages.title: Marks are exclusive
pages.text: A maid listens to $(l)either$() work targets $(l)or$() fluid targets, never both.$(br2)Applying fluid marks clears her work block / input / output, and vice versa. Switch back to the other mode and re-apply to change your mind.
